name: Stellarator optimization with differentiable and ML tools
summary: Stellarator coil and shape optimization uses adjoint or automatic differentiation and surrogate models over a large 3D parameter space.

name: Disruption prediction and plasma control with ML
summary: Tokamak disruption predictors and deep-RL magnetic controllers (e.g. on TCV) apply ML to real-time control where first-principles models are too slow.

name: ML surrogates and control in fusion
summary: Neural surrogates of gyrokinetic fluxes accelerate transport modelling, and reinforcement learning has been used for tokamak shape control and disruption prediction.

name: Ab initio MD for warm dense matter
summary: Warm dense matter equations of state and conductivities are computed by finite-temperature DFT-MD and path-integral Monte Carlo, bridging condensed matter methods to plasma conditions.

name: Strongly coupled plasmas studied by MD
summary: The one-component plasma and Yukawa systems are benchmark MD systems, with melting at Γ≈175 (OCP) and dusty-plasma crystals; MD gives transport and equation of state where perturbation theory fails.

name: Particle pushers and MD integrators
summary: PIC particle pushing and MD both integrate N-body trajectories with time-reversible Verlet-like schemes; MD with Coulomb forces uses Ewald or PPPM mesh methods also used in PIC.

name: Path-integral Monte Carlo for dense plasmas
summary: Fermionic PIMC and the sign problem constrain what can be computed for hydrogen and electron gases at WDM conditions; restricted and permutation-blocking variants give benchmark equations of state.

name: Monte Carlo neutronics and alpha-particle transport
summary: Neutron transport, tritium breeding and shielding in fusion devices use Monte Carlo codes, and Monte Carlo Fokker–Planck operators model fast-alpha slowing down.

name: Fokker–Planck collisions and Monte Carlo operators
summary: Coulomb collisions are a Fokker–Planck diffusion in velocity space, implemented by Monte Carlo binary-collision models (Takizuka–Abe) in PIC, equivalent to a Langevin stochastic process.

name: Radiation-hydrodynamics codes for ICF
summary: ICF design relies on multi-physics finite-volume or Lagrangian hydrodynamics coupled to radiation transport and shock-capturing schemes to model implosions and Rayleigh–Taylor growth.

name: Particle-in-cell simulation of wakefields
summary: PIC codes, often with boosted frames and quasi-static or envelope reductions, are the primary design tool for wakefield accelerators, whose bubble regime was found through simulation.

name: Divergence-free constraint and conservative MHD solvers
summary: Numerical MHD needs constrained transport, Godunov/Riemann solvers and divergence cleaning to preserve ∇·B=0; these schemes were developed for MHD and spread to astrophysical fluid codes.

name: Spectral direct numerical simulation of MHD turbulence
summary: Pseudo-spectral DNS is the main tool to test anisotropic cascade and critical-balance predictions; resolution limits restrict inertial range and Reynolds number, linking to astrophysical turbulence reviews.

name: Vlasov solvers and spectral methods
summary: Vlasov–Maxwell is solved by semi-Lagrangian, spectral (Hermite) and discontinuous-Galerkin schemes; recurrence and filamentation in velocity space limit resolution, and symplectic or structure-preserving integrators conserve invariants.

name: Boris pusher and symplectic integrators
summary: The Boris algorithm advances charged particles in E and B volume-preservingly with long-term stability, a precursor of modern structure-preserving integrators used in particle-in-cell codes.

name: Kramers–Kronig dispersion relations in plasma response
summary: Causality of the plasma dielectric response implies analyticity in the upper half ω-plane and Kramers–Kronig relations linking reactive and dissipative (Landau) parts.

name: Landau contour and plasma dispersion function
summary: Landau damping arises from the pole in the Vlasov dispersion integral; Landau's analytic-continuation prescription (deforming the contour) gives the Fried–Conte plasma dispersion function Z, a Faddeeva/error-function relative.

name: Diffusive shock acceleration power-law spectrum
summary: Diffusive shock acceleration yields a power-law spectrum from a Bessel/Green's-function-type transport problem and compression-ratio dependence; the shared paper reflects asymptotic and special-function methods in acceleration theory.

name: MHD stability as Sturm–Liouville / self-adjoint problem
summary: Linear ideal MHD is a self-adjoint force operator problem, so the energy principle δW and normal-mode spectrum follow from variational Sturm–Liouville-type theory.

name: Dispersion relations from linearized PDEs
summary: Plasma waves and instabilities are found by Fourier–Laplace transforming linearized fluid or Vlasov equations; the initial-value problem and Green's-function causality (Bers–Briggs) distinguish absolute from convective instability.

name: Self-adjoint force operator and spectral theorem
summary: The MHD force operator is Hermitian on a Hilbert space with energy inner product, giving real ω² and a spectrum with discrete and continuous parts (Alfvén and slow continua), with non-normal subtleties in flows.

name: Van Kampen modes and continuous spectrum
summary: Van Kampen's treatment of linearized Vlasov uses singular eigenfunctions of a continuous spectrum, with Landau damping appearing as phase mixing; the Vlasov operator is non-self-adjoint in general.

name: Frozen-in flux as Lie dragging of a 2-form
summary: Ideal MHD induction is Lie transport of the magnetic flux 2-form, and helicity is a differential-form integral; this geometric view clarifies the Cauchy solution and topological constraints.

name: Langmuir probes and plasma diagnostics
summary: Diagnostics such as Langmuir probes, Thomson scattering and interferometry rely on Debye sheath physics and detector noise limits; probe I–V curves infer density and temperature.

name: Structure functions and spectral inference of turbulence
summary: Solar wind turbulence exponents are estimated from spacecraft time series using structure functions and power spectra, with finite-sample and intermittency biases requiring statistical care.

name: Quasi-symmetry and conserved canonical momentum
summary: Quasi-symmetry in stellarators makes |B| symmetric in Boozer coordinates, so a Noether-type canonical momentum is conserved and guiding-centre orbits are confined like in tokamaks; omnigeneity generalizes this.

name: Axisymmetry gives conserved toroidal angular momentum
summary: Toroidal axisymmetry of a tokamak yields conservation of canonical toroidal angular momentum, confining particle orbits and underpinning neoclassical theory; stellarators lack this, hence 3D optimization.

name: Magnetic helicity and cross-helicity conservation
summary: Ideal MHD has conserved helicity invariants arising from relabelling symmetry of the fluid Lagrangian (Noether), constraining reconnection, dynamos and turbulent cascades.

name: Adiabatic invariants from approximate symmetry
summary: The magnetic moment and other adiabatic invariants are Noether-type conserved quantities of averaged Lagrangians with a slow-variable approximate symmetry; guiding-centre theory uses Lie-transform perturbation of the Hamiltonian structure.

name: Dynamo as symmetry-breaking of field
summary: Dynamos spontaneously break symmetries of the flow, such as reflection and time-reversal in geodynamo reversals, and the α-effect needs broken mirror symmetry (helicity); dynamo onset resembles a bifurcation with a growth-rate order parameter.
breaks: Dynamo growth is a kinematic linear instability, not an equilibrium ordered phase; no Goldstone modes in the usual sense.

name: Debye screening and Meissner/Higgs screening
summary: Debye screening gives a Yukawa-type potential with length λ_D, analogous to the finite penetration depth of magnetic fields in superconductors and the massive gauge boson range in the Higgs phase.
breaks: Debye screening is a thermal static effect, not a symmetry-breaking vacuum condensate, and the screening is electric rather than magnetic.

name: Plasma frequency and Higgs/Anderson mass generation
summary: Anderson noted that Coulomb long-range interaction turns the gapless Goldstone-like phonon into a gapped plasmon, the prototype of the Higgs mechanism; gauge field gives photon effective mass, as in plasma screening.
breaks: The plasma has no spontaneously broken local gauge symmetry; the photon mass is an effective in-medium dispersion, with the rest frame privileged.

name: Gyro-Bohm scaling and dimensionless confinement scaling
summary: Tokamak confinement scalings use Kadomtsev's constraint and Buckingham π to reduce parameters to ρ*, β, ν*; gyro-Bohm transport scales as ρ*χ_Bohm, enabling extrapolation to ITER.

name: Sweet–Parker scaling with Lundquist number
summary: The Sweet–Parker inflow rate follows from mass and flux balance, giving a scaling in Lundquist number S; plasmoid instability sets a critical S≈10^4 beyond which rate becomes S-independent.

name: Kolmogorov-style dimensional spectra for MHD turbulence
summary: Iroshnikov–Kraichnan and Goldreich–Sridhar spectra are derived by constant-flux dimensional arguments and critical balance, extending Kolmogorov scaling to magnetized fluids.

name: Plasma parameters as dimensionless groups
summary: Plasma regimes are classified by dimensionless numbers such as the plasma parameter, Lundquist number, beta and normalized gyroradius; similarity scaling lets lab experiments emulate astrophysical plasmas.

name: Adiabatic invariants as action variables
summary: The magnetic moment, bounce invariant J and flux invariant are action integrals of near-periodic motion, conserved to all orders in the slow-variation parameter under averaging.

name: Vlasov equation as Liouville flow
summary: The collisionless Vlasov equation is Liouville's theorem for the single-particle distribution function in phase space, with Poisson-bracket form and Hamiltonian field structure.

name: Guiding-centre Hamiltonian dynamics
summary: Guiding-centre motion is derived via Hamiltonian and Lagrangian averaging (Littlejohn, Lie-transform perturbation theory), preserving the symplectic structure and giving adiabatic invariants.

name: Radiation belts and three adiabatic invariants
summary: Trapped radiation-belt particles carry three adiabatic invariants (μ, J, Φ) from separation of gyro, bounce and drift timescales, a nearly integrable Hamiltonian system; radial diffusion breaks the third.

name: Gyrokinetics from Lagrangian field theory
summary: Modern gyrokinetics is derived from a phase-space Lagrangian with Lie-transform and variational methods, ensuring exact conservation laws via Noether's theorem.

name: Variational MHD equilibrium and stability
summary: MHD equilibrium extremizes energy at fixed constraints and stability follows from the energy principle δW, a Rayleigh–Ritz variational method; Grad–Shafranov describes axisymmetric equilibria.

name: MHD as continuum mechanics
summary: MHD applies continuum conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy to a conducting fluid with added magnetic stress.

name: MHD as fluid mechanics plus Lorentz force
summary: Ideal MHD is Euler or Navier–Stokes flow coupled to induction and the Lorentz force; vorticity and magnetic-field equations share the same frozen-in structure.

name: Alfvén waves as tension waves; Kelvin circulation
summary: Frozen-in flux parallels Kelvin's circulation theorem and vorticity transport; magnetic tension gives Alfvén waves like waves on a string, extending Euler flow.
breaks: Magnetic field adds anisotropic restoring force, so waves are not isotropic.

name: Parker wind as transonic nozzle flow
summary: Parker's solar wind is a de Laval-nozzle type steady flow with a critical sonic point; gravity and geometry replace the nozzle area change.
breaks: Wind is heated and magnetised, and the solar wind is collisionless with non-fluid effects.

name: Laser-plasma hydrodynamic instabilities
summary: Laser-driven ablation and shock-accelerated interfaces in laser plasmas realise classic interfacial instabilities (RT, RM, KH) under extreme conditions.

name: Rayleigh–Taylor in ICF implosions
summary: Rayleigh–Taylor and Richtmyer–Meshkov instabilities at the ablation front and fuel–shell interface limit capsule compression and ignition; classical growth rates are modified by ablation.

name: Convection-driven dynamos
summary: Rotating Rayleigh–Bénard convection drives geodynamo and solar dynamo flows, with helical convective motions supplying the α-effect.

name: MHD instabilities as magnetised RT/KH
summary: Interchange instability is Rayleigh–Taylor with effective gravity from field curvature; magnetic tension modifies Kelvin–Helmholtz thresholds and Chandrasekhar's magnetised convection.

name: Kinetic vs fluid instability analyses
summary: Normal-mode dispersion analysis and Nyquist criteria developed for plasma kinetic instabilities (two-stream, Penrose) parallel hydrodynamic shear and stratified-flow stability; the two-stream instability resembles Kelvin–Helmholtz.
breaks: Kinetic resonance with particle velocities has no fluid counterpart; fluid models lack velocity-space instabilities.

name: Ion-acoustic and Kelvin–Helmholtz in plasmas
summary: Kelvin–Helmholtz and Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities occur at magnetopause and in laser plasmas, with magnetic shear and finite Larmor radius modifying growth.

name: Plasma turbulence and fluid turbulence
summary: Drift-wave turbulence has cascades, intermittency and zonal-flow formation analogous to 2D fluid turbulence, mirrored by Hasegawa–Mima and Charney–Hasegawa–Mima equations.
breaks: Kinetic effects, resonant wave-particle interaction and non-adiabatic electrons have no fluid analogue.

name: Turbulent dynamo and mean-field theory
summary: Turbulent flows stretch, twist and fold field lines, giving small-scale dynamos and mean-field α-effect; the shared accretion-disk paper links turbulence, MRI and transport.

name: Kolmogorov cascade to MHD cascade
summary: Hydrodynamic energy cascade and Kolmogorov scaling generalize to MHD via Iroshnikov–Kraichnan and Goldreich–Sridhar theories, with Alfvén-wave interactions and anisotropy.
breaks: Magnetic field imposes anisotropy and non-local interactions; no isotropic Kolmogorov scaling exists in strong mean field.

name: MHD turbulence extends Kolmogorov theory
summary: Critical balance and anisotropic cascades in MHD turbulence extend Kolmogorov phenomenology, with magnetic energy and cross-helicity as additional invariants.
breaks: Strong mean field makes cascade anisotropic; scaling differs from isotropic Kolmogorov.

name: Shock jump conditions as conservation laws
summary: Rankine–Hugoniot conditions are mass, momentum and energy conservation across a discontinuity; collisionless shocks satisfy them via field-mediated dissipation instead of collisions.

name: Lorentz force and Coriolis force
summary: In a rotating frame the Coriolis force has the same form as the magnetic Lorentz force (Larmor's theorem), giving inertial waves and gyration analogous to cyclotron motion.
breaks: Coriolis force is mass-proportional and charge-independent; the centrifugal term has no magnetic counterpart.

name: Field-line flow as Hamiltonian system, KAM surfaces
summary: Magnetic field lines in toroidal geometry obey Hamiltonian equations with toroidal angle as time. Nested flux surfaces are KAM tori; resonant perturbations create islands and chaotic field lines.

name: Particle trapping and quasilinear resonance overlap
summary: Nonlinear Landau damping and particle trapping in a wave potential produce pendulum-like islands in phase space; overlapping waves yield Chirikov chaos underlying quasilinear diffusion.

name: Adiabatic invariant breakdown and chaos
summary: Magnetic moment conservation fails via resonance overlap or field-line curvature where gyroradius approaches field scale, producing chaotic scattering in current sheets and tail pitch-angle diffusion.

name: Nonlinear wake waves and wave breaking
summary: Plasma wakes are nonlinear Langmuir waves whose steepening and wave-breaking limit sets accelerating gradients, comparable to nonlinear wave steepening and soliton formation in dispersive media.
breaks: Wakefields are driven, relativistic and not integrable; breaking is not soliton formation.

name: Ion-acoustic solitons and KdV
summary: Weakly nonlinear ion-acoustic waves reduce to the KdV equation via reductive perturbation, giving solitons; Washimi–Taniuti derivation was a landmark. Alfvén waves yield DNLS.

name: Plasmoid chain formation as pattern formation
summary: Plasmoid instability of reconnection current sheets spontaneously produces hierarchical island chains from a tearing instability, analogous to pattern-forming instabilities.
breaks: Tearing is driven by free magnetic energy in a topological change; there is no Turing-type wavelength selection by diffusion.

name: Landau damping and Kuramoto synchronization
summary: Kuramoto oscillators with a frequency distribution obey a Vlasov-like continuum equation; incoherent-state stability and decay of the order parameter mirror Landau damping, as does the Case–Van Kampen analysis.
breaks: Kuramoto coupling is mean-field on a circle with no spatial structure; Kuramoto-model Landau damping is for non-smooth distributions.

name: Dust crystal lattice phonons
summary: Dusty-plasma crystals support lattice phonons observable by video microscopy; they are screened-Coulomb (Yukawa) chains and lattices with normal modes, allowing atomic-scale dynamics at the particle level.

name: Plasma oscillation as collective normal mode
summary: Langmuir oscillation at ω_p is a collective harmonic mode of displaced electron sheets, and plasma waves are dispersive normal modes of a continuum of coupled oscillators.
breaks: Long-range Coulomb coupling gives non-local dispersion and Landau damping not present in lattice chains.

name: Magnetosonic and acoustic waves
summary: Fast magnetosonic waves are sound waves stiffened by magnetic pressure; the Alfvén wave is a string wave along field lines, with dispersion from impedance-like medium properties.
breaks: Anisotropic propagation and three wave branches, unlike isotropic sound.

name: Ponderomotive force and Kapitza pendulum
summary: A charged particle in a rapidly oscillating field feels an effective ponderomotive potential, the same averaging that stabilizes the Kapitza pendulum's inverted position.

name: Parametric instabilities and Mathieu resonance
summary: Parametric decay instabilities in laser-plasma and plasma waves are three-wave coupled-mode versions of parametric resonance (Mathieu), with pump threshold set by damping.

name: Partial coherence suppresses instabilities
summary: Random phase plates and induced spatial incoherence reduce speckle-driven filamentation and parametric instabilities in laser plasmas by controlling coherence.

name: Interferometry for plasma density
summary: Interferometers measure line-integrated density through the plasma refractive index. Mach–Zehnder and two-colour interferometry are standard on tokamaks and laser plasmas.

name: Faraday rotation and magnetized-plasma birefringence
summary: A magnetized plasma is birefringent, with O and X modes and Faraday rotation of linear polarization. Used for polarimetry of tokamak currents and astrophysical fields; matches magneto-optic effects in crystals.

name: Plasma as electrodynamic medium
summary: A plasma is a medium with a frequency- and wavevector-dependent dielectric function from free charges. Skin depth, cutoff and reflection by the ionosphere follow from electrodynamics.

name: Maxwell equations underlying plasma waves
summary: Plasma waves follow from Maxwell's equations closed with a plasma current response; the dielectric tensor turns the wave equation into the dispersion relations of Langmuir, EM, and whistler modes.

name: Wave heating and current drive
summary: Electron cyclotron, ion cyclotron and lower-hybrid heating rely on waveguide and transmission-line technology, with gyrotrons as sources and wave propagation set by the magnetized-plasma dispersion relation.

name: EM waves in plasma: cutoff and skin depth
summary: Electromagnetic waves in a plasma have a cutoff at the plasma frequency and evanescent skin depth below it, like waveguide cutoff modes. Plasma-filled waveguides share the same dispersion form.

name: MHD as Maxwell with displacement current dropped
summary: MHD uses Ampère's law without displacement current and Faraday's law with Ohm's law. This gives induction equation, frozen-in flux and magnetic pressure and tension from the Maxwell stress tensor.

name: Magnetic energy release and Poynting flux
summary: Reconnection converts stored magnetic energy to flow and heat; field energy density and Poynting flux from Maxwell theory account for energy budgets, and Ohm's law breaks flux freezing.

name: Gauge choice in gyrokinetics and Vlasov–Maxwell
summary: Vlasov–Maxwell and gyrokinetic theory use scalar and vector potentials, with Coulomb gauge and Lagrangian/Hamiltonian formulations. Gauge invariance underlies canonical momentum conservation and the ponderomotive force.

name: E×B drift from field transformation
summary: The E×B drift is the velocity of the frame where E vanishes, following from the Lorentz transformation of fields. Invariants E·B and E²−c²B² determine when such a frame exists.

name: Debye screening as screened Poisson
summary: Debye shielding is Poisson's equation with a mobile-charge response, giving the screened (Yukawa) potential rather than Coulomb. Conductors in electrostatics are the infinite-density limit.

name: Dielectric response and screening in dusty plasma
summary: Dust grains charge and polarize in the plasma, and screened Coulomb (Yukawa) interactions follow from the dielectric response. Charged dust dynamics ties electrostatics to space plasmas.
breaks: Dust charge is not fixed; it varies with the plasma currents, and the interaction is non-reciprocal in flowing plasma.

name: Drifts from static field geometry
summary: Gradient-B and curvature drifts and magnetic mirrors arise from non-uniform static magnetic fields computed from Biot–Savart and Ampère. Adiabatic invariants link to the magnetic moment of current loops.

name: Magnetic fields and guiding-centre motion
summary: Lorentz force in static magnetic fields gives gyration, gradient and curvature drifts, and mirror forces. These follow from magnetostatic field geometry and the dipole moment of gyrating charges.

name: Dipole field of planetary magnetospheres
summary: Planetary fields are expanded in multipoles, with the dipole dominant. The dipole geometry sets L-shells, mirror points and radiation-belt trapping, with the magnetopause deforming it.

name: Intense lasers driving plasma
summary: High-power laser technology (chirped-pulse amplification, ultrashort pulses) supplies the drivers for laser–plasma physics. The plasma then acts as a nonlinear optical medium.

name: Ponderomotive force and Kerr nonlinearity in filaments
summary: Relativistic and ponderomotive self-focusing in plasma parallels Kerr self-focusing and filamentation in fibres and bulk media, with critical power thresholds and soliton-like channels.
breaks: Plasma nonlinearity is non-local and saturates via cavitation; Kerr nonlinearity is local and bound-electron.

name: Plasma as gain medium and X-ray lasers
summary: Laser-produced plasmas serve as gain media for soft X-ray lasers via collisional excitation, and free-electron lasers share synchrotron-radiation physics with plasma-accelerator-driven sources.

name: Surface plasmons and resonance absorption
summary: Surface plasmon polaritons in metals and resonance absorption at the critical density in laser plasmas both come from a Drude-type epsilon crossing zero, with a resonant collective electron oscillation.
breaks: Laser plasma is hot, inhomogeneous and nonlinear with density gradients; metal plasmons are cold, linear, bound to sharp interfaces.

name: Drude metal as cold plasma
summary: The free-electron Drude dielectric function of metals is the cold-plasma dielectric function. Bulk and surface plasmons are Langmuir-type oscillations, and epsilon-near-zero media exploit the plasma cutoff.

name: Laser beam smoothing and cross-beam energy transfer
summary: Optical frequency conversion (KDP harmonics) and beam smoothing deliver uniform UV drive in ICF. Cross-beam energy transfer is a stimulated Brillouin process.

name: Parametric instabilities as nonlinear optics
summary: Stimulated Raman and Brillouin scattering and two-plasmon decay are three-wave parametric processes, analogous to optical parametric amplification and stimulated scattering in nonlinear media. Relativistic self-focusing parallels Kerr self-focusing.

name: Topological waves in magnetized plasma
summary: Magnetized plasma, with gyrotropic dielectric tensor, breaks time reversal like magneto-optic photonic crystals. Topological edge modes (Parker et al.) can arise in continuous plasma, analogous to photonic quantum Hall.
breaks: Plasma is continuous and dispersive, so the topological invariant needs regularization and bulk-edge correspondence is subtle.

name: Plasma physics reliance on CPA lasers
summary: Chirped-pulse amplification, developed in optics, opened petawatt-class plasma experiments, including wakefield acceleration and ion acceleration.

name: Ultrafast pulses and relativistic laser-plasma
summary: Chirped-pulse amplification enabled relativistic intensities. High-harmonic generation on solid-plasma surfaces (relativistic oscillating mirror) is the plasma counterpart of gas-phase attosecond HHG.

name: Wakefield as Cherenkov wake
summary: A relativistic driver excites a wake in plasma at phase velocity equal to the driver velocity, a Cherenkov-type process. Transition radiation is used to diagnose the accelerated beams.

name: Cherenkov emission as beam-plasma instability
summary: Wave–particle resonance at ω=k·v is the Cherenkov condition. Landau damping and the beam-plasma instability are the collective version of Cherenkov emission of Langmuir waves.

name: Antenna coupling and heating of plasma
summary: Antenna and waveguide launching of ion-cyclotron, lower-hybrid and helicon waves uses radiation and coupling theory. Cutoffs and resonances in plasma determine accessibility.

name: Radiation from laser-driven electrons
summary: Electrons oscillating in intense laser fields emit nonlinear Thomson/Compton radiation and radiation-reaction losses. The Larmor and Liénard formulas govern emission and the damping force in ultra-intense regimes.
